qt: to the Commission Ewa Zajączkowska-Hernik (PfE) Subject:

The EU rail freight sector has been in a very difficult economic situation for several years. The Commission should uphold the common market and the principles of equal competition. Meanwhile, the Ukrainian State Railways Ukrzaliznytsia established Ukrainian Railways Cargo Poland in 2024, which operates freight services on European markets. I ask: Has the Commission examined the granting of a licence to Ukrainian Railways Cargo Poland, which is part of the state-owned capital group of Ukraine, and compliance with EU legislation on unbundling and separation of accounts?
at: (English version) to the Commission Ewa Zajączkowska-Hernik (PfE) (15 July 2026) Subject: Operating rules for third country subsidiaries on the EU rail market The EU rail freight sector has been in a very difficult economic situation for several years. The Commission should uphold the common market and the principles of equal competition. Meanwhile, the Ukrainian State Railways Ukrzaliznytsia established Ukrainian Railways Cargo Poland in 2024, which operates freight services on European markets. I ask: Has the Commission examined the granting of a licence to Ukrainian Railways Cargo Poland, which is part of the state-owned capital group of Ukraine, and compliance with EU legislation on unbundling and separation of accounts? (9 November 2026) A similar question on the same company has already been raised and answered (Reference: EPQ — E-225/26 (1)). The granting of a licence is the responsibility of a licensing authority designated by each Member State. The Commission can confirm that the Polish railway regulator (Urząd Transportu Kolejowego — UTK) issued a licence to Ukrainian Railways Cargo Poland in 2024 and that this licence became active as of 2 September 2026. The licensing conditions, requirements and procedures are laid down in the directive 2012/34/EU (2) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/171 (3). These requirements are transposed into national legislation. In order to obtain a licence, a railway undertaking must demonstrate that it will at any time be able to meet the requirements relating to good repute, financial fitness, professional competence and cover for its civil liability. An undertaking which fulfils these requirements shall be authorised to receive a licence. Compliance with the EU rail market legislation and, more specifically, ensuring fair competition and an efficient rail market in the EU Member States, is the prerogative of national rail regulatory bodies. National rail regulatory bodies are also empowered to carry out audits or initiate external audits of infrastructure managers, service facility operators and railway undertakings to verify compliance with the accounting separation provisions. In the case of vertically integrated undertakings these powers extend to all legal entities within the group. The Commission actively monitors the situation in each Member State and maintains regular exchanges with the national rail regulatory bodies. For the time being, the Commission is not aware of any non-compliance in this case.
